title: Porous-silicon reusable seed: one CZ crystal, fifty DRAM wafers
idea: Periodic-table walk, Si (14): anodize a seed wafer into a double-layer porous Si, grow a 5-8 um epitaxial device layer, build or bond, then cleave at the weak porous layer and re-polish the seed for 20-50 reuses; the carrier can be reclaimed or upgraded-metallurgical Si because DRAM devices use only the top ~1 um.
why: Cuts electronic-grade CZ crystal (and Spruce Pine quartz crucibles, pulling energy) per wafer by ~10-30x; attacks quartz chokepoint and energy intensity.

title: Reusable silicon-nitride crucible replaces Spruce Pine quartz in Czochralski pulling
idea: Periodic-table walk, Si+N (14,7): pull DRAM crystals from dense reaction-bonded Si3N4 crucibles with a sacrificial Si3N4 powder release coat (borrowed from multicrystalline solar casting); no cristobalite devitrification, so one crucible survives ~10 pulls with continuous recharge, and oxygen for gettering is dosed via O2 in the Ar ambient instead of crucible dissolution.
why: Removes most high-purity-quartz demand (>80% from one US district); slight N doping (1e14-1e15 cm^-3) even helps vacancy control in DRAM wafers.

title: Aluminum-core wordlines for arrays built entirely at back-end temperatures
idea: Periodic-table walk, Al (13): when the cell array is made of oxide-channel transistors at <=400 C, wordlines no longer need to survive 1000 C, so use low-temperature CVD Al (dimethylaluminum hydride, fluorine-free) cores with a 2 nm TiN skin instead of W or Ru.
why: Eliminates W (~80% China) and WF6 from the array; bulk resistivity 2.7 vs 5.3 uOhm-cm allows ~2x longer wordlines and fewer drivers, shrinking periphery.

title: Rutile TiO2 dielectric templated by antimony-doped tin-oxide electrodes
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ti (22) with Sn (50): SnO2 is isostructural with rutile, so a conductive Sb:SnO2 bottom electrode templates rutile TiO2 (k~90-110) at <=350 C ALD, replacing Ru/RuO2 templates and Hf/Zr high-k; a 1 nm Al-doped TiO2 cap holds leakage.
why: Hits the k~70 target from fact 1 with Ti and Sn only: ~2x Cs at the same aspect ratio or AR 70->~35; Hf-free, Ru-free.

title: Hafnium-free antiferroelectric zirconia capacitor storing switched charge
idea: Periodic-table walk, Zr (40): use pure tetragonal ZrO2's field-induced double hysteresis loop, biasing the plate at the loop midpoint so each write swings through one antiferroelectric loop and releases ~20-30 uC/cm2 instead of ~5-8 uC/cm2 linear charge; zero-field relaxation avoids ferroelectric imprint.
why: 2-3x effective Cs at AR<=40 with Zr (~100x more abundant than Hf, whose world output is ~70-80 t/yr).

title: Indium- and gallium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain-cell transistor
idea: Periodic-table walk, Zn (30): replace IGZO in 2T0C gain cells with amorphous Zn-Sn-O (Zn:Sn ~2:1) by ALD (diethylzinc + TDMA-Sn), with Si or Al doping to pin oxygen vacancies for <1e-19 A/um off-current.
why: Removes Ga (~98% China primary) and In (~60% China) from capacitor-less oxide DRAM; two abundant metals only.

title: p-type tin-monoxide CMOS periphery stacked over the array
idea: Periodic-table walk, Sn (50): pair n-type ZTO with p-type SnO (hole mobility 1-5 cm2/Vs) to build complementary sense-amp drivers and decoders at <=400 C directly above the cell array, moving part of the 49% periphery off silicon wafer area.
why: ~25-35% less silicon wafer area per bit, hence fewer wafers, crucibles and EUV passes; Sn is abundant and already an EUV-source consumable.

title: Iron-silicon Heusler electrodes for cobalt-free, platinum-free magnetic tunnel junctions
idea: Periodic-table walk, Fe (26): grow D03 Fe3Si (or Fe2MnSi) epitaxial electrodes on MgO, couple synthetic antiferromagnets through Cr instead of Ru, and pin with MnN antiferromagnets instead of PtMn/IrMn.
why: Swaps Co (DRC), Pt/Ir (South Africa) and Ru for Fe, Si, Mn, Cr, N in any spin-based DRAM substitute; abundant-only magnetic stack.

title: Mn3Sn antiferromagnetic bit: written by torque, read by tunneling
idea: Periodic-table walk, Mn (25): store bits in the chiral spin order of the Weyl antiferromagnet Mn3Sn, switched by spin-orbit torque and read by tunneling magnetoresistance in Mn3Sn/MgO/Mn3Sn; no stray field, so cells pack without magnetic crosstalk, and THz dynamics allow sub-ns writes with magnetic-class endurance.
why: No capacitor charge wall and no refresh; only Mn and Sn, no Co, Pt or rare earths.

title: Chromium orbital-Hall torque layer replaces platinum, tungsten and tantalum
idea: Periodic-table walk, Cr (24) and Ti (22): light 3d metals have large orbital Hall conductivity; a Cr or Ti line under a thin Ni orbital-to-spin converter switches the free layer by orbital torque, replacing the Pt/W/Ta heavy-metal write line of SOT memory.
why: Removes W, Pt and Ta from spin-orbit-torque memory; lower-resistivity write lines cut write energy ~2x.

title: Barrierless copper-aluminum intermetallic local interconnect
idea: Periodic-table walk, Cu (29) with Al: use ordered intermetallics such as CuAl2, whose short electron mean free path keeps resistivity flat down to ~10 nm and which do not diffuse into dielectrics, so no TaN/Ta or Co liners; deposit by co-sputter plus 400 C anneal or subtractive Cl2 etch.
why: Removes W, Ta, Co and Ru from the tightest DRAM pitches; ~2x lower line resistance than W at 12 nm.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM pools: let 77 K shrink the capacitor
idea: Periodic-table walk, N (7): run rack-scale memory pools at 77 K in LN2 or cryocooled sleds, where access-transistor leakage falls >1e6x and retention rises from 64 ms to hours, so cells can be designed with a 1-1.5 fF capacitor (AR ~15) and no refresh.
why: Deletes the most tool- and material-intensive steps (deep mold etch, high-k stacks) and refresh energy (46 fJ/bit); nitrogen comes from air.

title: Nanoporous-carbon ionic double-layer storage node
idea: Periodic-table walk, C (6): replace the dielectric capacitor with an electric double layer, a 5 nm-pore CVD carbon electrode filled with a nonvolatile ionic liquid or solid polymer electrolyte; ~10 uF/cm2 times internal pore area gives ~20-50 fF in a 30x30x300 nm volume, and ion transit across 5 nm pores is ~10-30 ns.
why: Breaks the k/AR charge wall using only C, H, N, O: 4-10x Cs at AR ~10, no Hf/Zr ALD.

title: Bistable buckled aluminum-nitride nanobeam as a leak-free bit
idea: Periodic-table walk, Al+N (13,7): a pre-stressed 100 nm AlN beam buckles into one of two stable states; a piezoelectric kick (ns, since resonance is ~GHz) flips it and capacitive sensing reads it; there is no contact, so wear stays at resonator-class (>1e15 cycles) and nothing leaks.
why: No capacitor, no access-transistor leakage tail, no refresh; Al, N and Si only, and no high-k or W.

title: Point-of-use helium recapture loops on every tool
idea: Periodic-table walk, He (2): the element is irreplaceable in a few steps, so fit each remaining He user (cryopumps, leak checks, CZ purge blends) with polymer-membrane plus PSA recapture and local recompression, returning >90% to a fab ring main instead of venting.
why: Cuts virgin helium demand ~90% amid the Qatar outage (~30% of world supply offline).

title: Unbundle hafnium from nuclear zirconium with a U.S. separation hub
idea: Periodic-table walk, Hf (72): hafnium exists only as a by-product of nuclear-grade Zr purification, so fund a Hf/Zr solvent-extraction plant fed by Florida-Georgia-Virginia heavy-mineral-sand zircon, with chipmaker offtake contracts and a strategic reserve.
why: Decouples high-k/HZO supply (~70-80 t/yr world) from reactor demand; ~2-3x supply resilience.

title: Gallium harvested from alumina-refinery Bayer liquor
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ga (31): install amidoxime ion-exchange columns on Bayer liquor (~100-200 ppm Ga) at U.S. and allied alumina refineries, turning a waste stream into tens of tonnes per year for oxide channels and GaN periphery power.
why: China holds ~98% of primary Ga under export controls; this route could cover U.S. semiconductor demand.

title: Germanium recovered from Alaskan zinc concentrate and coal fly ash
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ge (32): recover Ge domestically from Red Dog zinc concentrates now shipped abroad and from Ge-rich fly ash via tannin precipitation and solvent extraction, dedicated to SiGe superlattices for 3D DRAM.
why: Removes export-control exposure for the SiGe sacrificial layers that 26+ tier 3D DRAM needs.

title: Fab-side closed tungsten loop from exhaust and spent targets
idea: Periodic-table walk, W (74): cryo-trap unreacted WF6 from W-CVD exhaust and redistill it, and send spent targets, shields and chamber scrap to zinc-process reclamation under a fab take-back contract.
why: W is ~80% China; recapture could cut virgin W per wafer by ~50%.

title: Boron-carbon hardmask replaces tungsten-doped carbon for deep etches
idea: Periodic-table walk, B (5): PECVD boron-rich carbon (30-60% B from B2H6 plus C3H6) gives B-C bonds whose etch resistance rivals W-doped carbon in high-aspect-ratio etches, and it strips in O2/Cl2.
why: Removes W from hardmasks for capacitor and contact etches; the U.S. is a top-two borate producer.

title: Epitaxial nickel-disilicide buried bitlines for vertical-channel cells
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ni (28): cubic NiSi2 is lattice-matched to Si (0.4% mismatch), so form single-crystal NiSi2 at pillar bases by templated Ni diffusion, then overgrow Si to make 4F2 vertical-channel transistors over a metallic buried bitline.
why: Replaces W/TiN buried bitlines (no WF6) and enables 4F2 cells; Ni is abundant (U.S./Canada).

title: MgB2 superconducting flux-loop memory at 20 K, helium-free
idea: Periodic-table walk, Mg (12): build persistent-current flux-quantum cells with MgB2 (Tc 39 K) junctions and kinetic inductors, operated at 20 K by cryocooler or liquid H2 instead of liquid He, as a zero-static-power working memory in cryogenic AI pods.
why: Zero refresh, near-zero energy per bit; avoids Nb (~85% Brazil) and He (Qatar); Mg and B are abundant.

title: Closed fluorine loop: scrubber fluorspar back to on-site F2
idea: Periodic-table walk, F (9): capture HF and fluorocarbon exhaust in Ca(OH)2 scrubbers as synthetic CaF2, convert it back to HF, and electrolyze KF.2HF on-site to F2 for chamber cleans, replacing NF3.
why: Removes NF3 (GWP 17,200, few suppliers) and virgin fluorspar (China/Mexico) dependence; F2 has GWP 0.

title: Fluorine-free molybdenum buried wordlines from oxychloride ALD
idea: Periodic-table walk, Mo (42): deposit buried-channel wordlines by ALD Mo from MoO2Cl2 + H2 (chloride, no WF6); Mo's ~11 nm electron mean free path beats W's ~15.5 nm in 10 nm trenches, and without fluorine attacking the gate oxide the TiN barrier can be thinned or dropped.
why: Kills W (~80% China) and WF6; the U.S. is a top-two Mo producer (Colorado); ~20-30% lower wordline resistance.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as a plasma-free capacitor mold
idea: Periodic-table walk, Al+O (13,8): deposit 2-3 um Al over the array, nano-imprint pore seeds aligned to storage-node contacts, and anodize in oxalic/sulfuric acid so vertical pores self-grow at AR >100; open the barrier in H3PO4 and ALD the electrode/dielectric stack inside.
why: Replaces the C4F8/CHF3 high-aspect-ratio oxide etch (the most fluorine- and capital-intensive DRAM step) with room-temperature electrochemistry; AR 100+ gives ~7 fF.

title: Carbon molds etched by oxygen with sulfur sidewall passivation
idea: Periodic-table walk, C+S (6,16): form capacitor holes in an amorphous-carbon mold using O2 plasma with COS/SO2 additive, whose sulfur-carbon sidewall film replaces fluorocarbon polymer passivation for straight ~80:1 holes; after electrode deposition the mold is simply ashed in O2.
why: Removes C4F8/CHF3 and HF mold strip; ashing instead of a wet release avoids pillar collapse and rinse water.

title: Doped single-crystal silicon pillar as a metal-free storage electrode
idea: Periodic-table walk, Br (35): etch degenerately P-doped (>1e20 cm^-3) Si pillars with HBr/Cl2/O2 (bromide-oxide passivation, no fluorine), wrap them in ALD high-k and a TiN plate, so the pillar itself is the bottom electrode with no oxide mold, no TiN bottom electrode and no HF removal.
why: Drops ~10 steps plus the fluorocarbon etch and HF wet; stiff crystalline pillars tolerate higher AR before collapse (<=10% depletion C loss).

title: KOH-on-(110)-silicon crystal-plane trenches for capacitor fins
idea: Periodic-table walk, K (19): on (110) wafers, alkaline etchants cut near-perfect vertical {111} walls at 100-600:1 plane selectivity, so one DUV line mask along <112> yields atomically smooth deep trench/fin capacitors; TMAH substitutes for KOH where alkali contamination matters.
why: Swaps EUV-pitch plasma HAR etch for wet crystal anisotropy, fluorine-free, at roughly 1/20 the etch-tool capital.

title: Water-soluble salt release layer for stacking oxide memory tiers
idea: Periodic-table walk, Na+Cl (11,17): evaporate a NaCl film on a reusable carrier, seal it with ALD Al2O3, build an oxide-transistor DRAM tier at <=400 C (below NaCl's 801 C melt), bond it onto the stack, and dissolve the salt in water to release it.
why: Tier-by-tier 3D DRAM without HF/XeF2 sacrificial release and without consuming a Si wafer per tier; carrier reused indefinitely.

title: Strontium-catalyzed native-oxide desorption replaces the HF-last clean
idea: Periodic-table walk, Sr (38): before epitaxy or gate stacks, deposit ~0.5 monolayer Sr in vacuum and anneal at ~750-800 C; Sr reduces SiO2 to volatile SiO plus SrO and leaves an oxide-free (2x1) surface, borrowing the SrTiO3-on-Si MBE trick.
why: Removes the HF dip on which every front-end clean depends, plus its rinse water.

title: Vapor-deposited zinc-imidazolate framework as a dry photoresist
idea: Periodic-table walk, Zn (30): grow ZIF-8-type zinc 2-methylimidazolate films by CVD/ALD; EUV or e-beam exposure changes linker bonding so films develop in vapor or non-fluorinated solvent, with no PFAS photoacid generator, no fluorinated surfactant and no spin-coat waste.
why: PFAS-free patterning; Zn has high EUV absorption (lower dose); eliminates the ~95% of spin-coated resist that is discarded.

title: Iodine-loaded fluorine-free chemically amplified EUV resist
idea: Periodic-table walk, I (53): build resists from iodinated phenolic polymers with iodonium/sulfonium photoacid generators carrying non-fluorinated anions (camphorsulfonate, carboxylates); iodine's high EUV cross-section and secondary electrons make up for the weaker acid.
why: Removes PFAS photoacids; ~2-3x higher photon absorption lowers dose, raising wafers per hour on the single-supplier EUV tool.

title: Titanium and PEEK wetted paths for a fluoropolymer-free fab
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ti (22): once HF is gone from the fab, the main reason for PFA/PTFE plumbing disappears, so distribute UPW and oxidizing acids in electropolished titanium (passive TiO2 film) and use PEEK/high-purity polypropylene for reducing acids, solvents and slurries.
why: Fluoropolymers are the largest PFAS mass in a fab; removes that lifecycle liability with abundant Ti.

title: Robot-swapped recyclable aluminum chamber liners instead of NF3 cleans
idea: Periodic-table walk, Al (13): deposition chambers get thin anodized-Al liners that collect film deposits and are swapped through the load lock every N wafers, then remelted (secondary Al takes ~5% of primary energy) with residues separated as dross; sold as liner-as-a-service.
why: Eliminates NF3/fluorine in-situ cleans and their GWP; automated swaps keep uptime.

title: Molten calcium chloride electrolysis turns ordinary sand into silicon
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ca+Cl (20,17): electro-deoxidize pressed SiO2 pellets from ordinary sand at ~850 C in molten CaCl2 (FFC route), with the salt recycled, and feed the Si powder to zone refining and CZ recharge.
why: Bypasses the arc furnace (11-13 kWh/kg plus coke) and Siemens chlorosilane steps; any sand works, no fluorides, U.S.-sited.

title: Rice-husk biogenic silica feeds synthetic Czochralski crucibles
idea: Periodic-table walk, Si+O (14,8): acid-leach rice-husk ash (~90% amorphous SiO2) with HCl/citric acid, calcine it to high-purity silica, and slip-cast crucibles with an inner sol-gel synthetic-silica layer; U.S. rice states supply millions of tonnes of husk.
why: Breaks the >80% Spruce Pine high-purity-quartz chokepoint with a renewable domestic feedstock, purified without HF.

title: Boron cluster molecules for fluorine-free p-type doping
idea: Periodic-table walk, B (5): replace BF3/BF2+ implants with octadecaborane (B18H22) cluster implantation or monolayer doping from boronic-acid esters plus spike anneal, with no fluorine co-implant and no BF3 gas cabinets.
why: Removes a major fluorinated implant gas; cluster beams give ~10-20x effective low-energy dose rate, so fewer implanters.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers by doping-selective electrochemical etch
idea: Periodic-table walk, P (15): grow a 30-100-tier all-silicon superlattice of n+ (P) and p (B) layers instead of Si/SiGe, then remove the p layers laterally in TMAH under electrochemical bias, where the n layers passivate at the p-n junction.
why: Avoids export-controlled Ge; an unstrained homo-Si stack can pass 100 tiers with no HF/CF4 lateral recess (fact 2).

title: Ozone-gas and UV dry stripping to cut ultrapure water
idea: Periodic-table walk, O (8): replace sulfuric-peroxide resist strips and organic cleans with UV-activated O3 gas and humidified-ozone single-wafer dry oxidation, keeping wet steps only for metal and particle removal.
why: Cuts DRAM-fab UPW use ~30-50% and acid consumption; fluorine-free.

title: On-site electrochemical persulfate regeneration closes the sulfuric loop
idea: Periodic-table walk, S (16): electrolyze spent sulfuric acid on boron-doped-diamond anodes to regenerate peroxydisulfate continuously, so the cleaning oxidant is remade on-site rather than consuming fresh H2SO4 and H2O2.
why: ~90% less sulfuric/peroxide purchase and wastewater; fluorine-free; uses only S, O, H and C/B electrodes.

title: Supercritical-CO2 drying to push capacitor pillars past AR 100
idea: Periodic-table walk, C+O (6,8): perform post-etch rinse and dry in supercritical CO2 with a non-fluorinated co-solvent, removing the liquid meniscus whose capillary force topples 60-75:1 pillars, and recover CO2 from industrial streams.
why: Direct attack on the capacitor charge wall (AR ~115 needed), plus less water and IPA.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling in electrostatic chucks replaces helium
idea: Periodic-table walk, H (1): feed H2 (thermal conductivity 0.18 W/mK, above He's 0.15) at 5-20 Torr behind wafers in etch/CVD chucks; sccm flows stay below the flammability limit with N2-diluted exhaust, and supply comes from on-site electrolysis.
why: Removes one of the largest fab helium uses during the Qatar outage; H2 comes from water.

title: Electroless nickel-boron plating fills contacts without WF6
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ni (28): activate silicided contact bottoms and plate Ni-B bottom-up from an aqueous NiSO4 plus dimethylamine-borane bath at 60-80 C with a suppressor additive, then anneal to form NiSi at the interface.
why: Replaces CVD tungsten (WF6, China W) for cell and periphery contacts with a low-capital wet bench; fluorine-free.

title: Ceria-free iron-oxide Fenton-assisted CMP slurry with magnetic recovery
idea: Periodic-table walk, Fe (26): swap rare-earth ceria abrasives for Fe3O4 nanoparticles plus in-situ Fenton chemistry (Fe2+/H2O2 hydroxyl radicals) that softens oxide surfaces, and recover the magnetic particles from slurry waste with magnets; post-clean in dilute HCl.
why: Removes the CeO2 rare-earth chokepoint and fluorinated surfactants; recycles ~60-80% of abrasive.

title: Chlorination plus ligand-exchange thermal ALE for 3D DRAM lateral recess
idea: Periodic-table walk, Cl (17): recess TiN, ZrO2 and Al2O3 laterally inside 3D DRAM tiers by cyclic thermal atomic-layer etching, chlorinating with SOCl2 or BCl3 then removing the surface with TiCl4 or trimethylaluminum ligand exchange, avoiding the HF step of standard thermal ALE.
why: Self-limiting, isotropic, angstrom-precise cavities across 100+ tiers (fact 2 blocker), fluorine-free.

title: Tin-oxide spacers etched by hydrogen for fluorine-free multiple patterning
idea: Periodic-table walk, Sn (50): use ALD SnO2 as the SADP/SAQP spacer and hardmask, etched in H2/CH4 plasma (volatile SnH4) with high selectivity to Si, SiO2 and carbon, while Si and carbon are etched in Cl2/HBr/O2, a full pitch-quartering flow without CF chemistry; Sn is reclaimed from exhaust.
why: Removes CF4/CHF3 spacer etches and lets DUV SAQP displace some of the 5-7 EUV layers (single-supplier chokepoint).
